items.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: I especially was fond of the Chicago guys. Joe Sullivan, Teschemacker, Bud, those guys, that whole school.

ctx.x: Was it mostly the non-musicians that started that? Was it the writers and the critics?

Many musicians felt, younger ones, yeah I think they had a lot to do with it. They fanned the flames. They saw good copy. Divide and— bebop versus— they even use to have those concerts at Birdland. The moldy figs. Here’s Max Kaminsky and Edmond Hall and who else and whatever. And over here are Diz and Bird or whatever it is. You know, and this is going to get people to come in. It’s sort of like that trumped up, like the boxing thing, you know when they all, “I can knock ‘em flat” and all that stuff. You know,…
Now you, from telling me your schedule, are quite a globe trotter. I mean this music has gotten you around to some different places. What is the European thing for this music?
